en.name: Pea shoots
en.summary: Pea shoots are the tender tips and young leaves of the pea plant, stir-fried with garlic in seconds. No figure is published for them, so treat them like bagged salad leaves: about 2–4 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, kept dry and loosely bagged.
en.pantry: Pea shoots have no meaningful room-temperature life. They are the softest growth on the plant, thin-leaved and full of water, and in a warm kitchen a bunch wilts within a couple of hours. There is no pantry figure and none should be assumed. Get them home cold and into the crisper, and ideally cook them the same day.
en.fridge: Keep pea shoots dry and loosely bagged in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where about 2–4 days is the working limit — borrowed from bagged salad greens, since nothing is published for 豆苗. Dryness is everything here: any water trapped on the leaves turns them to slime overnight. Rooted punnets, sold still growing in their tray, last noticeably longer than cut shoots, and you can cut what you need and leave the rest growing. Do not wash until you cook.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for pea shoots and freezing them is not worth doing. Their whole appeal is a fresh, sweet, almost squeaky crispness that lasts about thirty seconds in a hot wok; freezing bursts the cells and hands you back a dark green sludge. Nothing unsafe happens, but nothing usable comes out. Buy a punnet rather than a big bunch if you cannot use it quickly.
spoilage: Slimy leaves stuck together in a wet clump
Yellowing or translucent leaves, or blackened stem ends
A sour or fermented smell when the bag is opened
Liquid pooling in the bottom of the bag or punnet
tips: Buy a rooted punnet if you want a few days rather than a few hours.
Keep them dry and loose; never bag them damp.
Wash and spin dry only what you are about to cook.
Stir-fry with garlic for well under a minute — pea shoots collapse the moment they are overdone.

faq.q: How long do pea shoots last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 2–4 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, dry and loosely bagged. That figure is borrowed from bagged salad greens; none is published for pea shoots.
There is no timeline and no point. Freezing destroys the crispness that is the only reason to buy them.

faq.q: Why do pea shoots go slimy overnight?
faq.a: Water trapped on very thin leaves. Store them dry and loosely packed, and wash only just before cooking.

faq.q: Are rooted pea shoots better than cut ones?
faq.a: For storage, yes. A punnet still growing in its tray keeps noticeably longer, and you can cut what you need and leave the rest alive.

zh.name: 豆苗
zh.summary: 豆苗是豌豆植株的嫩尖和幼葉，蒜炒幾秒鐘就能上桌。它沒有公布的保存數據，可以比照袋裝沙拉葉來看：4°C 以下冷藏約 2～4 天，保持乾燥、鬆鬆裝袋。
zh.pantry: 豆苗沒有什麼可用的常溫保存期。它是整株植物上最柔嫩的部分，葉薄又多水，在溫暖的廚房裡兩三個小時就萎了。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。請保冷帶回家放進蔬果保鮮室，最好當天就煮。
zh.fridge: 請保持乾燥、鬆鬆裝袋，放在 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，約 2～4 天是工作上限——這是比照袋裝沙拉葉而來，因為豆苗本身沒有任何公布的數據。乾燥在這裡是一切：葉片上只要留住水，一夜之間就會爛成黏糊。連根帶盆販售、還在生長的盆裝豆苗，明顯比切下來的耐放，而且可以要多少剪多少、其餘繼續長。要煮之前才洗。
zh.freezer: 豆苗沒有冷凍保存期限，冷凍也不值得。它的價值全在那股清甜、幾乎會發出聲音的脆度——那份脆度在熱鍋裡也只撐得住大約三十秒；冷凍會撐破細胞，還給你的是一團深綠色的爛泥。這不會有安全問題，但也沒有任何能用的東西。用不完的話，請買盆裝而不是一大把。
spoilage: 葉片泛黃或變得半透明，莖的切口發黑
打開袋子聞到酸味或發酵味
袋底或盆底積出一灘水
tips: 想放幾天而不是幾小時，就買連根的盆裝豆苗。
保持乾燥、不要壓實；絕對不要濕著裝袋。
只洗當餐要煮的量，洗完務必甩乾。
蒜炒不到一分鐘就好——豆苗一過火就整個垮掉。

faq.q: 豆苗放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、保持乾燥鬆鬆裝袋，約 2～4 天。這個數字是比照袋裝沙拉葉而來；豆苗本身沒有公布的數據。
沒有對應的期限，也沒有意義。冷凍會毀掉那份脆度，而那是買它的唯一理由。

faq.q: 豆苗為什麼一個晚上就爛掉了？
faq.a: 因為水留在極薄的葉片上。請保持乾燥、鬆鬆裝袋，要煮之前才洗。

faq.q: 盆裝豆苗比切好的好嗎？
faq.a: 以保存來說是的。連根還在生長的盆裝明顯更耐放，而且可以要多少剪多少，其餘繼續活著。
